title: Heat Pump Rebates in Oshawa 2026: Rebates and the Oshawa Power Service Area
desc: Oshawa heat pump rebates for 2026 under Home Renovation Savings: 59% of homes predate 1981, and the rebate depends on your current heating fuel.
badge: Up to $7,500 for an air-source heat pump
lead: Oshawa has 66,635 households, 59% in homes built before 1981. Oshawa Power is your electric utility, but the heat pump rebate comes from Enbridge Gas and Save on Energy.
cards_heading: What Home Renovation Savings pays for a heat pump in Oshawa
cards_intro: We re-read the program's heat pump page and its requirements document on October 3, 2026. No home energy assessment is needed for this stream, but a participating HVAC contractor and written pre-approval are.

cards.title: Air-source, electric, oil, propane or wood heat
cards.note: For a cold-climate air-source heat pump replacing electric resistance, oil, propane or wood as the main heat. A 3-ton system pays $3,750 and 6 tons or more reaches the cap.

cards.title: Air-source, Enbridge gas heat
cards.note: For homes primarily heated by an Enbridge gas furnace or boiler. The cap is reached at 4 tons.

cards.title: Ground-source
cards.note: For electric, oil, propane or wood homes. Gas homes get a flat $3,000. The system must be a full installation sized to the home's load.

cards.title: Rented heat pump
cards.note: Rentals are eligible for any primary heating fuel: $500 per ton for air-source, up to $2,000, or a flat $3,000 for ground-source.

cards.title: More than one outdoor unit
cards.amount: Up to three units, one rebate
cards.note: If several outdoor units are needed to heat the whole home, their tons add up and one rebate is paid on the total, for example 3 + 3 tons for $7,500.

cards.title: One rebate, pre-approved
cards.note: One rebate per home. The contractor needs written pre-approval before installing, files the post-installation application within 30 days, and the cheque arrives within 60 days of approval.

after_cards: The requirements document lists no end date, but the program's other streams close in late 2026, so check the program page before you sign a contract. Pre-approval is mandatory: an installation done first earns nothing.
sections: The 2021 Census counts 16,595 owner-occupied detached houses built before 1981 in Oshawa, 74% of households in an eligible type and 64% owning. 6.3% report needing major repairs. Oshawa has 5,360 semi-detached and 6,490 row households.
Utility does not set the rebate

Oshawa is served by Oshawa Power (Oshawa PUC Networks), not Elexicon. The program is open to homes connected to the Ontario grid through any local utility, apart from Cornwall Electric. What matters for the rebate is your primary heating fuel before the install.

An electrically heated home qualifies if its primary heating equipment is electric resistance, such as baseboards, and a wood-heated home qualifies on photos of its stove. Both can keep the old system as backup. Neither backup is rebated. Photos of baseboards are needed in at least three areas.

No installation can begin until the program has approved the pre-installation application in writing. An Oshawa owner who accepts a quote and lets the crew start before approval loses the rebate. Ask the contractor for a written start date that follows the approval.

An Oshawa home heated mainly by wood qualifies at the $1,250-per-ton rate, with sizing options C and D only, and the wood stove may stay as backup. The pre-installation photos must show the stove. The program counts the stove as the primary heating equipment only if that is how the home is actually heated, so be honest in the application.

The contractor files within 30 days of installation, with the final itemized invoice, photos of the equipment and thermostat, and measure details. The cheque arrives within 60 days of approval. Ask for copies of both applications.
claim_steps: Find out your main fuel and ask for the approval before any work starts.
Confirm eligibility on the program's short form and get the list of participating HVAC contractors.
Choose a contractor from that list. Ask for a load calculation and the NRCan sizing tool form for each outdoor unit.
Wait for written pre-approval before any installation starts.
After the install, check that the contractor files the post-installation application within 30 days, with the final itemized invoice and photos.
